source_text: Καὶ γὰρ μυῖαι ἐμπεσοῦσαι μύρῳ, καὶ ἐναποπνιγεῖσαι, ἀσχήμονα τοῦ ἡδέος ἐκείνου χρίσματος, τήν τε ὄψιν, καὶ τὴν χρίσιν ἐργάζονται· σοφίας δὲ καὶ ἀφροσύνης οὐδὲν ἐν ταὐτῷ μεμνῆσθαι προσῆκον. Ὁ μέν γε σοφὸς ἑαυτὸν ἐπὶ δεξιὰ τῶν πραγμάτων ὁδηγεῖ· ἄφρων δὲ εἰς ἀριστερὰ ἀπονένευκεν, οὐδ᾽ ἔστιν ὅτε καλῶν ὁδηγῷ πραγμάτων ἀφροσύνῃ χρήσεται. Μάταια δὲ αὐτοῦ καὶ τὰ ἐνθυμήματα, ἀφροσύνης ἀναπεπλησμένα. Εἰ δὲ καὶ πνεῦμά σοί ποτε, ὦ φίλος, πολέμιον προσπέσοι, ἔνστηθι ἐῤῥωμένως, γινώσκων ὡς καὶ πολλῶν ἁμαρτημάτων πλῆθος Θεὸς ἱλάσασθαι δύναται. Τυράννου δὲ ἔργα ταῦτα, καὶ πατρὸς πάσης πονηρίας· τὸν μὲν ἄφρονα εἰς ὕψος αἴρεσθαι, τὸν πλούσιον δὲ φρονήσει ταπεινοῦσθαι· καὶ δούλους μὲν ἁμαρτιῶν ἐπὶ ἵππον φερομένους, ἄνδρας δὲ ἱεροὺς βαδίζοντας ἀτίμως ὁρᾶσθαι, τῶν πονηρῶν γαυρουμένων.
thought_title: Flies in ointment; wisdom versus folly in leadership and danger
orientation: Solomon continues his teaching, using the image of flies spoiling ointment to illustrate how folly corrupts wisdom, then contrasting the wise who turn right with the foolish who turn left, and warning about a hostile spirit and the inversion of proper order under tyrants.
pass_a_gloss: For indeed flies having fallen into myrrh, and having been suffocated in it, work an unseemly appearance and the anointing of that sweet ointment; but of wisdom and folly it is not fitting to remember anything together in the same way. The wise man indeed guides himself to the right of matters; but the fool has inclined toward the left, nor is there any time when he will use folly with a good guide of matters. And his reasonings are futile, filled full of folly. But if also a hostile spirit should ever fall upon you, O friend, stand firm confidently, knowing that God is able to be propitiated for the multitude even of many sins. These are works of a tyrant, and of the father of all wickedness: to lift up the fool to a height, but to humble the rich man with prudence; and to see slaves of sins being carried upon a horse, but holy men walking to be seen dishonorably, the wicked exulting.

choices.why: Literal rendering of the Ecclesiastes 10:1 image; 'myrrh' keeps the specific ointment term.
Captures the compound verb 'suffocated in' the substance; not merely 'drowned'.

choices.term: ἀσχήμονα τήν τε ὄψιν καὶ τὴν χρίσιν ἐργάζονται
choices.english: work an unseemly appearance and the anointing
choices.why: Preserves the double object (appearance and anointing) and the verb 'work/produce'.
rejected: spoil the look and the anointing

choices.term: σοφίας δὲ καὶ ἀφροσύνης οὐδὲν ἐν ταὐτῷ μεμνῆσθαι προσῆκον
choices.english: but of wisdom and folly it is not fitting to remember anything together in the same way
choices.why: Renders the negative infinitive with 'fitting' and the phrase 'in the same' (ἐν ταὐτῷ) as 'together in the same way'.
rejected: wisdom and folly should not be mentioned together

choices.term: ὁ μέν γε σοφὸς ἑαυτὸν ἐπὶ δεξιὰ τῶν πραγμάτων ὁδηγεῖ
choices.english: The wise man indeed guides himself to the right of matters
choices.why: Keeps the reflexive 'himself', the directional 'to the right', and 'of matters' (τῶν πραγμάτων).

choices.english: but the fool has inclined toward the left
choices.why: Uses 'inclined' for ἀπονένευκεν (perfect of ἀπονεύω) and 'toward the left' for εἰς ἀριστερά.

choices.term: πνεῦμά σοί ποτε, ὦ φίλος, πολέμιον προσπέσοι
choices.english: a hostile spirit should ever fall upon you, O friend
choices.why: Renders the optative condition 'should ever fall upon' and the vocative 'O friend'.
rejected: if an enemy spirit attacks you

choices.gloss: God is able to be propitiated for the multitude even of many sins
choices.why: Uses 'propitiated' for ἱλάσασθαι to keep the theological sense of appeasing God.

choices.term: Τυράννου δὲ ἔργα ταῦτα, καὶ πατρὸς πάσης πονηρίας
choices.english: These are works of a tyrant, and of the father of all wickedness
choices.why: Identifies the described inversions as tyrant's works and links 'father of all wickedness' to the devil.

choices.term: δούλους μὲν ἁμαρτιῶν ἐπὶ ἵππον φερομένους
choices.english: slaves of sins being carried upon a horse
choices.why: Literal: 'slaves of sins' (genitive) and present participle 'being carried'.

choices.term: ἄνδρας δὲ ἱεροὺς βαδίζοντας ἀτίμως ὁρᾶσθαι
choices.english: holy men walking to be seen dishonorably
choices.why: Preserves the passive infinitive 'to be seen' and adverb 'dishonorably'.

pass_b_english: Flies fall into myrrh and suffocate there, spoiling both the look and the application of that sweet ointment. It is not fitting to remember wisdom and folly together in the same way. The wise person indeed guides himself toward the right in his dealings, but the fool has inclined toward the left, and he never takes folly as his guide to good deeds. The fool's thoughts are futile, stuffed full of folly. If a hostile spirit should ever fall upon you, my friend, stand firm, knowing that God is able to forgive even a multitude of many sins (Ecclesiastes 10:4 LXX). Such inversions are the works of a tyrant, and of the father of all wickedness: the fool is lifted high, while the rich person is humbled in prudence; slaves of sin are seen being carried on horseback, while holy men are seen walking on foot without honor, and the wicked exult (Ecclesiastes 10:5-7 LXX).

problems.quote: while holy men walk dishonorably (Ecclesiastes 10:5-7 LXX)
problems.why: The closing clause, 'the wicked exulting/priding themselves', is missing from the English.
problems.fix: …while holy men are seen walking without honor, and the wicked swagger proudly.

problems.quote: God is able to be propitiated for the multitude even of many sins
problems.why: God is the agent who propitiates or forgives. The English passive makes God the one appeased, which reverses the agency.
problems.fix: God is able to forgive even a multitude of many sins.

problems.quote: there is no time when folly will use a good guide for affairs
problems.source_quote: οὐδ᾽ ἔστιν ὅτε καλῶν ὁδηγῷ πραγμάτων ἀφροσύνῃ χρήσεται
problems.why: The sense is that the fool never takes folly as a guide to good deeds. The English drops the fool as subject and mislocates folly.
problems.fix: and he never takes folly as his guide to good deeds.

problems.quote: the look and the fragrance of that sweet anointing
problems.source_quote: ἀσχήμονα τοῦ ἡδέος ἐκείνου χρίσματος, τήν τε ὄψιν, καὶ τὴν χρίσιν ἐργάζονται
problems.why: χρίσιν is the anointing itself, not its fragrance; both look and anointing of the ointment are made unseemly.
problems.fix: making unseemly both the appearance and the anointing of that sweet ointment.
problems.ruling: τὴν χρίσιν means the anointing or application, not fragrance. 'Fragrance' adds a sense the Greek lacks, and the unseemly appearance and anointing are the point.

edits.old: It is not fitting to speak of wisdom and folly in the same breath.
edits.new: It is not fitting to remember wisdom and folly together in the same way.

edits.old: The wise person indeed guides himself toward the right in his dealings, but the fool has inclined toward the left, and there is no time when folly will use a good guide for affairs.
edits.new: The wise person indeed guides himself toward the right in his dealings, but the fool has inclined toward the left, and he never takes folly as his guide to good deeds.

edits.old: The fool's thoughts are empty, stuffed full of folly.
edits.new: The fool's thoughts are futile, stuffed full of folly.

edits.old: stand firm, knowing that God is able to be propitiated for the multitude even of many sins (Ecclesiastes 10:4 LXX).
edits.new: stand firm, knowing that God is able to forgive even a multitude of many sins (Ecclesiastes 10:4 LXX).

edits.old: Such inversions are the works of a tyrant, and of the father of all wickedness: the fool is lifted high, while the rich person is humbled in prudence; slaves of sin are seen being carried on horseback, while holy men walk dishonorably (Ecclesiastes 10:5-7 LXX).
edits.new: Such inversions are the works of a tyrant, and of the father of all wickedness: the fool is lifted high, while the rich person is humbled in prudence; slaves of sin are seen being carried on horseback, while holy men walk dishonorably, and the wicked exult (Ecclesiastes 10:5-7 LXX).

fixed: Changed 'speak of ... in the same breath' to 'remember ... together in the same way' to match μνημονεύειν προσῆκον.
Corrected 'there is no time when folly will use a good guide for affairs' to 'he never takes folly as his guide to good deeds' so the fool remains subject and folly is the rejected guide.
Changed 'empty' to 'futile' to render Ματαῖα accurately.
Changed 'God is able to be propitiated' to 'God is able to forgive' to make God the active agent of ἱλάσασθαι.
Added the missing clause 'and the wicked exult' from τῶν πονηρῶν γαυρουμένων.
Gloss: changed 'making unseemly both the appearance and the anointing' to 'working an unseemly appearance and the anointing' to reflect ἐργάζονται.

problems.quote: the fragrance of that sweet anointing
problems.source_quote: ἀσχήμονα τοῦ ἡδέος ἐκείνου χρίσματος, τήν τε ὄψιν, καὶ τὴν χρίσιν ἐργάζονται
problems.why: χρίσιν is the anointing or application, not the smell; both the look and the use are made unseemly.
problems.fix: spoiling both the look and the application of that sweet ointment.
problems.ruling: τὴν χρίσιν means the anointing or application, not scent. "Fragrance" is not in the Greek, so the English adds a sense the source doesn't have.

problems.source_quote: ἄνδρας δὲ ἱεροὺς βαδίζοντας ἀτίμως ὁρᾶσθαι
problems.why: ἀτίμως means 'without honor, in disgrace'. 'Dishonorably' suggests the holy men act badly, but the point is that they are shown no honor.
problems.fix: holy men are seen walking on foot without honor
problems.ruling: ἀτίμως modifies βαδίζοντας ὁρᾶσθαι: holy men are seen walking in disgrace, not acting shamefully.

fixed: Changed 'fragrance' to 'application' to reflect χρίσιν (the anointing/use) per source: 'τὴν χρίσιν ἐργάζονται'.
Changed 'walk dishonorably' to 'are seen walking on foot without honor' to reflect ἀτίμως ὁρᾶσθαι (seen in disgrace/without honor) and βαδίζοντας (walking on foot).
